purpose: Stability-based diagnostic (Hennig clusterwise Jaccard via fpc::clusterboot + fpc::prediction.strength) on the 25 SOM codebook vectors, addressing reviewer objection that the k=4 partition is unsupported by separation gap/silhouette. Read-only additive computation; no existing artifact modified.

neuron_to_regime_mapping.source: Recomputed deterministically: hclust(dist(codes,euclidean),ward.D2) |> cutree(k=4); EXACT match to neurons_in_cluster in output/som_metrics.json
neuron_to_regime_mapping.note: fpc::hclustCBI default scaling=TRUE re-standardizes columns and does NOT reproduce the paper; clusterboot/prediction.strength here use scaling=FALSE which reproduces the paper partition exactly (verified identical).

clusterboot.call: set.seed(456); clusterboot(codes, B=1000, distances=FALSE, bootmethod=boot, clustermethod=hclustCBI, method=ward.D2, k=4, scaling=FALSE, cut=number, count=FALSE)
clusterboot.hennig_2007_bands: >0.85 highly stable; 0.75-0.85 stable; 0.6-0.75 patterns but uncertain; <0.6 dissolved

prediction_strength.call: set.seed(456); prediction.strength(codes, Gmin=2, Gmax=6, M=100, clustermethod=hclustCBI, method=ward.D2, cut=number, scaling=FALSE, classification=centroid, cutoff=0.8)
prediction_strength.n_caveat: n=25 codebook vectors is small; per-k strengths are noisy and optimalk=1 is the expected outcome when no k>=2 clears the 0.8 cutoff. Report as corroborating that no strong multi-cluster split is recoverable by held-out prediction, consistent with the weak silhouette and gap=1; the k=4 choice is interpretive/operational, not separation-driven.

early_slope_imputation_bias.scaling_note: Task specified z=(x-med)/(IQR/1.349) -> +1.07. BUT the paper-operative early_slope_z (stored in feature_matrix.parquet) uses z=(x-med)/IQR (raw IQR, no 1.349) -> +0.79; verified by reproducing stored z exactly on non-zero values. The +0.79 value is what feeds the SOM.
early_slope_imputation_bias.imputed_z_vs_C1_centroid: imputed +0.79 is MORE positive than the C1 Slow-Decay centroid (+0.61); imputation actively pulls cells toward Slow Decay
early_slope_imputation_bias.verdict: MATERIAL (not marginal): 62.2% of the imputed-zero cohort lands in C1 Slow Decay; 34.3% of C1 is this cohort; imputed z (+0.79) exceeds the C1 centroid (+0.61), so structural-zero imputation is a non-trivial driver of Slow-Decay membership and should be disclosed.
